questions.q: Let $\overset{→}{a}, \overset{→}{b}$ and $\overset{→}{c}$ be three non-zero vectors such that $\overset{→}{b}$ and $\overset{→}{c}$ are non-collinear if $\overset{→}{a} + 5\overset{→}{b}$ is collinear with $\overset{→}{c}, \overset{→}{b} + 6\overset{→}{c}$ is collinear with $\overset{→}{a}$ and $\overset{→}{a} + \alpha\overset{→}{b} + \beta\overset{→}{c} = \overset{→}{0}$, then $\alpha + \beta$ is equal to
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given: $\overset{→}{a} + 5\overset{→}{b}$ is collinear with $\overset{→}{c}, \overset{→}{b} + 6\overset{→}{c}$ is collinear with $\overset{→}{a}$ and $\overset{→}{a} + \alpha\overset{→}{b} + \beta\overset{→}{c} = \overset{→}{0}$.

$⇒ \overset{→}{a} + 5\overset{→}{b} = \lambda\overset{→}{c} . . . \left(i\right)$

$⇒ \overset{→}{b} + 6\overset{→}{c} = \mu\overset{→}{a} . . . \left(ii\right)$

$⇒ \overset{→}{a} = \lambda\overset{→}{c} - 5\overset{→}{b} = \dfrac{\overset{→}{b} + 6\overset{→}{c}}{μ}$

$⇒ \lambda\overset{→}{c} - 5\overset{→}{b} = \dfrac{6}{μ}\overset{→}{c} + \dfrac{1}{μ}\overset{→}{b}$

Comparing both the sides,

$⇒ \mu = \dfrac{- 1}{5}, \lambda = -30$

Putting these values in equation \left(i\right)$

$⇒ \overset{→}{a} + 5\overset{→}{b} = - 30\overset{→}{c}$

$⇒ \overset{→}{a} + 5\overset{→}{b} + 30\overset{→}{c} = 0$

Comparing this equation with $\overset{→}{a} + \alpha\overset{→}{b} + \beta\overset{→}{c} = \overset{→}{0}.$

$⇒ \alpha =5, \beta =30$

$⇒ \alpha + \beta =35$

$

questions.q: Let $\overset{→}{a} = 5\overset{^}{i} - \overset{^}{j} - 3\overset{^}{k}$ and $\overset{→}{b} = \overset{^}{i} + 3\overset{^}{j} + 5\overset{^}{k}$ be two vectors. Then which one of the following statements is TRUE?
options: Projection of $\overset{→}{a}$ on $\overset{→}{b}$ is $\dfrac{- 13}{35}$ and the direction of~the projection vector is opposite to the direction of $\overset{→}{b}$
Projection of $\overset{→}{a}$ on $\overset{→}{b}$ is $\dfrac{- 17}{35}$ and the direction of the projection vector is opposite to the direction of $\overset{→}{b}$
Projection of $\overset{→}{a}$ on $\overset{→}{b}$ is $\dfrac{17}{35}$ and the direction of the projection vector is opposite to the direction of $\overset{→}{b}$
Projection of $\overset{→}{a}$ on $\overset{→}{b}$ is $\dfrac{13}{35}$ and the direction of the projection vector is opposite to the direction of $\overset{→}{a}$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given

$\overset{→}{a} = 5\overset{^}{i} - \overset{^}{j} - 3\overset{^}{k}$

So,~\left|\overset{→}{a}\right| = \sqrt{{5}^{2} + {1}^{2} + {3}^{2}} = \sqrt{35}$

$\overset{→}{b} = \overset{^}{i} + 3\overset{^}{j} + 5\overset{^}{k}$

So,~$\sqrt{{5}^{2} + {1}^{2} + {3}^{2}} = \sqrt{35}$

So,~$\overset{→}{a} \cdot \overset{→}{b} = 5 - 3 - 15 = - 13$

Now finding the projection of~$\overset{→}{a}$~on~$\overset{→}{b}$ using the formula we get,

$\overset{→}{a} \cdot \overset{→}{b}\left|\overset{→}{b}\right| = - \dfrac{13}{35}$

And projection of~$\overset{→}{b}$~on~$\overset{→}{a}$~is given by,

$\overset{→}{a} \cdot \overset{→}{b}\left|\overset{→}{a}\right| = - \dfrac{13}{35}$

questions.q: Let $\vec{a}=\hat{i}+2 \hat{j}+3 \hat{k}, \vec{b}=3 \hat{i}+\hat{j}-\hat{k}$ and $\vec{c}$ be three vectors such that $\vec{c}$ is coplanar with $\vec{a}$ and $\vec{b}$. If the vector $\vec{C}$ is perpendicular to $\vec{b}$ and $\vec{a} \cdot \vec{c}=5$, then $|\vec{c}|$ is equal to
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \overrightarrow{\mathrm{c}}=\lambda(\overrightarrow{\mathrm{b}} \times(\overrightarrow{\mathrm{a}} \times \overrightarrow{\mathrm{b}})) \\ & =\lambda((\overrightarrow{\mathrm{b}} \cdot \overrightarrow{\mathrm{b}}) \overrightarrow{\mathrm{a}}-(\overrightarrow{\mathrm{a}} \cdot \overrightarrow{\mathrm{b}}) \overrightarrow{\mathrm{b}}) \\ & =\lambda(11 \overrightarrow{\mathrm{a}}-2 \overrightarrow{\mathrm{~b}})=\lambda(11 \mathrm{i}+22 \mathrm{j}+33 \mathrm{k}-6 \mathrm{i}-2 \mathrm{j}+2 \mathrm{k}) \\ & =\lambda(5 \mathrm{i}+20 \mathrm{j}+35 \mathrm{k}) \\ & =5 \lambda(5 \mathrm{i}+4 \mathrm{j}+7 \mathrm{k}) \\ & =\text { Given } \overrightarrow{\mathrm{c}} \cdot \overrightarrow{\mathrm{a}}=5 \\ & =5 \lambda(1+8+21)=5 \quad=\lambda=\frac{1}{30} \\ & \Rightarrow \overrightarrow{\mathrm{c}}=\frac{1}{6}(\mathrm{i}+4 \mathrm{j}+7 \mathrm{k}) \\ & \overrightarrow{\mathrm{c}}=\frac{\sqrt{1+16+49}}{6}=\sqrt{\frac{11}{6}}\end{aligned}$

questions.q: Let $\overset{→}{a} = \overset{^}{i} - 2\overset{^}{j} + \overset{^}{k}$ and $\overset{→}{b} = \overset{^}{i} - \overset{^}{j} + \overset{^}{k}$, be two vectors. If $\overset{→}{c}$, is a vector such that $\overset{→}{b} \times \overset{→}{c} = \overset{→}{b} \times \overset{→}{a}$ and $\overset{→}{c} ⋅ \overset{→}{a} = 0,$ then $\overset{→}{c} ⋅ \overset{→}{b}$, is equal to.
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
$\overset{→}{a} \times \left(\overset{→}{b} \times \overset{→}{c}\right) = \overset{→}{a} \times \left(\overset{→}{b} \times \overset{→}{a}\right)
$⇒ - \left(\overset{→}{a} . \overset{→}{b}\right)\overset{→}{c} = \left(\overset{→}{a} . \overset{→}{a}\right)\overset{→}{b} - \left(\overset{→}{a} . \overset{→}{b}\right)\overset{→}{a}

Using given information~$\overset{→}{a} = \overset{^}{i} - 2\overset{^}{j} + \overset{^}{k}$~and~$\overset{→}{b} = \overset{^}{i} - \overset{^}{j} + \overset{^}{k}$~, we can write~$\overset{→}{a} . \overset{→}{b} = 4$,~$\overset{→}{a} . \overset{→}{a} = 6$
$⇒ - 4\overset{→}{c} = 6\left(\overset{^}{i} - \overset{^}{j} + \overset{^}{k}\right) -$4 \left(\overset{^}{i} - 2\overset{^}{j} + \overset{^}{k}\right)$
$⇒ - 4\overset{→}{c} = 2\overset{^}{i} + 2\overset{^}{j} + 2\overset{^}{k}$
$⇒ \overset{→}{c} = - \dfrac{1}{2} \left(\overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j} + \overset{^}{k}\right)
$⇒ \overset{→}{b} . \overset{→}{c} = - \dfrac{1}{2}.$

questions.q: Let the position vectors of the vertices $A, B$ and $C$ of a tetrahedron $A B C D$ be $\hat{\mathbf{i}}+2 \hat{\mathbf{j}}+\hat{\mathbf{k}}, \hat{\mathbf{i}}+3 \hat{\mathbf{j}}-2 \hat{k}$ and $2 \hat{i}+\hat{j}-\hat{k}$ respectively. The altitude from the vertex $D$ to the opposite face $A B C$ meets the median line segment through $A$ of the triangle $A B C$ at the point $E$. If the length of $A D$ is $\frac{\sqrt{110}}{3}$ and the volume of the tetrahedron is $\frac{\sqrt{805}}{6 \sqrt{2}}$, then the position vector of $E$ is
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution: Area of $\triangle \mathrm{ABC}=\frac{1}{2}|\overrightarrow{\mathrm{AB}} \times \overrightarrow{\mathrm{AC}}|=\frac{1}{2}|5 \hat{\mathrm{i}}+3 \hat{\mathrm{j}}+\hat{\mathrm{k}}|=\frac{1}{2} \sqrt{35}$ volume of tetrahedron $\begin{aligned} & =\frac{1}{3} \times \text { Base area } \times \mathrm{h}=\frac{\sqrt{805}}{6 \sqrt{2}} \\ & \frac{1}{3} \times \frac{1}{2} \sqrt{35} \times \mathrm{h}=\frac{\sqrt{805}}{6 \sqrt{2}} \\ & \mathrm{~h}=\sqrt{\frac{23}{2}} \end{aligned}\mathrm{AE}^2=\mathrm{AD}^2-\mathrm{DE}^2=\frac{13}{18} \therefore \mathrm{AE}=\sqrt{\frac{13}{18}}$\begin{aligned} & \overrightarrow{\mathrm{AE}}=|\mathrm{AE}| \cdot\left(\frac{\hat{\mathrm{i}}-5 \hat{\mathrm{k}}}{\sqrt{26}}\right) \\ & =\sqrt{\frac{13}{18}} \cdot\left(\frac{\hat{\mathrm{i}}-5 \hat{\mathrm{k}}}{\sqrt{26}}\right) \\ & =\sqrt{\frac{13}{18}} \cdot\left(\frac{\hat{\mathrm{i}}-5 \hat{\mathrm{k}}}{\sqrt{26}}\right)=\frac{\hat{\mathrm{i}}-5 \hat{\mathrm{k}}}{6} \\ & \text { P.V. of } \mathrm{E}=\frac{\hat{\mathrm{i}}-5 \hat{\mathrm{k}}}{6}+\hat{\mathrm{i}}+2 \hat{\mathrm{j}}+\hat{\mathrm{k}}=\frac{1}{6}(7 \hat{\mathrm{i}}+12 \hat{\mathrm{j}}+\hat{\mathrm{k}})\end{aligned}$$

Then the square of the length of the largest side of the triangle $\mathrm{ABC}$ is _______

questions.q: Let& $\overset{→}{a}, \overset{→}{b}$~and~$\overset{→}{c}$~be three unit vectors such that~\left|\overset{→}{a} - \overset{→}{b}\right|2 + \left|\overset{→}{a} - \overset{→}{c}\right|2 = 8$. Then~\left|\overset{→}{a} + 2\overset{→}{b}\right|2 + \left|\overset{→}{a} + 2\overset{→}{c}\right|2$& is equal to
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
& \left|\overset{→}{a}\right| = \left|\overset{→}{b}\right| = \left|\overset{→}{c}\right| = 1$

\left|\overset{→}{a} - \overset{→}{b}\right|2 + \left|\overset{→}{a} - \overset{→}{c}\right|2 = 8$

$⇒ 1 + 1 - 2\overset{→}{a} \cdot \overset{→}{b} + 1 + 1 - 2\overset{→}{a} \cdot \overset{→}{c} = 8$

$⇒ \overset{→}{a} \cdot \overset{→}{b} + \overset{→}{a} \cdot \overset{→}{c} = - 2$

Now \left|\overset{→}{a} + 2\overset{→}{b}\right|2 + \left|\overset{→}{a} + 2\overset{→}{c}\right|2$

$= \left|\overset{→}{a}\right|2 + 4\left|\overset{→}{b}\right|2 + 4\overset{→}{a} \cdot \overset{→}{b} + \left|\overset{→}{a}\right|2 + 4\left|\overset{→}{c}\right|2 + 4\overset{→}{a} \cdot \overset{→}{c}$

$= 2\left|\overset{→}{a}\right|2 + 4\left|\overset{→}{b}\right|2 + 4\left|\overset{→}{c}\right|2 + 4 \left(\overset{→}{a} \cdot \overset{→}{b} + \overset{→}{a} \cdot \overset{→}{c}\right)

$= 2 + 4 + 4 + 4 \left(- 2\right)$

$= 2

questions.q: If $\overset{→}{a} = 2\overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j} + 3\overset{^}{k}, \overset{→}{b} = 3\overset{^}{i} + 3\overset{^}{j} + \overset{^}{k}$~and $\overset{→}{c} = {c}_{1}\overset{^}{i} + {c}_{2}\overset{^}{j} + {c}_{3}\overset{^}{k}$~are coplanar vectors and $\overset{→}{a} \cdot \overset{→}{c} = 5, \overset{→}{b} ⊥ \overset{→}{c}$, then $122  \left({c}_{1} + {c}_{2} + {c}_{3}\right)& is equal to ______.$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
As the given vectors are coplanar, so& \left|$\begin{cases}2 & 1 & 3 \\ 3 & 3 & 1 \\ {c}_{1} & {c}_{2} & {c}_{3}\end{cases}$\right| = 0$

$⇒ 8{c}_{1} - 7{c}_{2} - 3{c}_{3} = 0 . . . \left(i\right)$

Also,~$\overset{→}{a} \cdot \overset{→}{c} =5 ⇒ 2{c}_{1} + {c}_{2} + 3{c}_{3} = 5 . . . \left(ii\right)$

and~$\overset{→}{b} \cdot \overset{→}{c} =0 ⇒ 3{c}_{1} + 3{c}_{2} + {c}_{3} = 0 . . . \left(iii\right)$

Solving the above three equations using Cramer's rule, we get,

$∆ = \left|$\begin{cases}8 \text{ and } - 7 \text{ and } - 3 \\ 2 \text{ and } 1 \text{ and } 3 \\ 3 \text{ and } 3 \text{ and } 1\end{cases}\right| = - 122$

${∆}_{1} = \left|$\begin{cases}0 \text{ and } - 7 \text{ and } - 3 \\ 5 \text{ and } 1 \text{ and } 3 \\ 0 \text{ and } 3 \text{ and } 1\end{cases}\right| = - 10$

${∆}_{2} = \left|$\begin{cases}8 \text{ and } 0 \text{ and } - 3 \\ 2 \text{ and } 5 \text{ and } 3 \\ 3 \text{ and } 0 \text{ and } 1\end{cases}\right| = 85$

${∆}_{3} = \left|$\begin{cases}8 \text{ and } - 7 \text{ and } 0 \\ 2 \text{ and } 1 \text{ and } 5 \\ 3 \text{ and } 3 \text{ and } 0\end{cases}\right| = - 225$

Hence,~$122\left({c}_{1} + {c}_{2} + {c}_{3}\right) =122\left(\dfrac{10}{122} - \dfrac{85}{122} + \dfrac{225}{122}\right) =150$

$

questions.q: $A \left(2, 6, 2\right), B  \left(-$4, 0, \lambda\right), $C\left($2, 3, - 1\right)$ and D\left($4, 5, 0\right), \left|\lambda\right| \le$5$~are the vertices of a quadrilateral $ABCD$. If its area is $18$ square units, then $5 - 6\lambda is equal to _____ .$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given:

$A \left(2, 6, 2\right), B \left(-$4, 0, \lambda\right), $C\left($2, 3, - 1\right)D\left(4, 5, 0\right)$

Area of quadrilateral~

=\dfrac{1}{2}\left|\overset{→}{AC} \times \overset{→}{BD}\right| =$18$

$⇒ \left|\overset{→}{AC} \times \overset{→}{BD}\right|36$

Now,

$\overset{→}{AC} \times \overset{→}{BD} = \left|$\begin{cases}\overset{^}{i} \text{ and } \overset{^}{j} \text{ and } \overset{^}{k} \\ 0 \text{ and } - 3 \text{ and } - 3 \\ 8 \text{ and } 5 \text{ and } - \lambda\end{cases}\right|$

$⇒ \overset{→}{AC} \times \overset{→}{BD} = \left(3\lambda + 15\right)\overset{^}{i} - \left(0 + 24\right)\overset{^}{j} + \left(0 + 24\right)\overset{^}{k}$

$⇒ \overset{→}{AC} \times \overset{→}{BD} = \left(3\lambda + 15\right)\overset{^}{i} - 24\overset{^}{j} + 24\overset{^}{k}$

So,

\left|\overset{→}{AC} \times \overset{→}{BD}\right| =36$

$⇒ $\sqrt{\left(3\lambda + 15\right)2 + \left(24\right)2 + \left(24\right)2} =$36$

$⇒ 9{λ}^{2} + 225 + 90\lambda = 1296 - 1152$

$⇒ 9{λ}^{2} + 90\lambda - 81 = 0$

$= {λ}^{2} + 10\lambda + 9 = 0$

$⇒ \lambda = - 1, - 9$

Since,

\left|\lambda\right| \le5 ⇒ \lambda = - 1$

Therefore,

$5 - 6\lambda = 5 - 6\left(-1\right) = 11$
